exposure: delivery mode (elective CD, unscheduled CD, vaginal delivery)
group B Streptococcus (GBS) intrapartum antibiotic prophylaxis (IAP) exposure
cohort: The study included 157,820 infants born between 2007-2015 within an integrated healthcare system, with data followed through 5 years of age.
finding: Both unscheduled cesarean delivery and GBS IAP exposure were independently associated with a significant increase in BMI during early childhood, compared to vaginal delivery or no IAP exposure, respectively.
mod_finding: Unscheduled cesarean delivery (with or without GBS IAP) was positively associated with higher BMI compared to vaginal delivery, but no BMI difference was observed between elective and unscheduled cesarean deliveries.
